result.feature_understanding: The admin login screen lets administrators sign in to the admin panel of the HKM Prasadam System. Testers must verify that only users with valid admin credentials can log in and that any invalid credentials are rejected. The screen uses the POST /api/admin/auth/login API to authenticate the user. The biggest risk is unauthorized access, so confirming proper authentication and error handling is critical. Also be sure to test the forgot‑password and token‑refresh endpoints to handle password reset scenarios.

failure_path_tests.title: API timeout: POST /api/admin/auth/login exceeds SLA
failure_path_tests.description: Simulate POST /api/admin/auth/login taking longer than the SLA threshold (e.g. 30 s). Verify the client receives a meaningful timeout error and the operation does not partially commit.
steps: Configure POST /api/admin/auth/login to respond after 30 s (mock/stub)
Trigger the feature flow
Verify the caller receives HTTP 504 or an explicit timeout error
Verify no partial data was written to the database
Verify a retry or circuit-breaker mechanism activates if configured
failure_path_tests.expected_result: Caller gets a safe timeout error; no partial state change; circuit breaker trips after N failures

failure_path_tests.title: Circuit breaker opens after repeated failures on /api/admin/auth/login
failure_path_tests.description: Repeatedly fail the downstream dependency to trigger the circuit breaker. Verify open-state fast-fail behaviour and eventual half-open recovery.
steps: Cause /api/admin/auth/login to return 500 for 5 consecutive calls
Verify the circuit breaker moves to OPEN state
Verify subsequent calls fail fast (< 100 ms) without hitting the dependency
Wait for the cooldown window, then send one request
Verify the circuit breaker enters HALF-OPEN and allows the probe request
Verify recovery to CLOSED state on a successful probe
failure_path_tests.expected_result: Circuit breaker opens, fast-fails, and recovers correctly

failure_path_tests.title: admin login screen test cases: DB failure mid-transaction rolls back cleanly
failure_path_tests.description: Simulate a DB constraint violation or connection drop mid-transaction. Verify the entire operation rolls back and no event is published.
steps: Begin the feature operation
Inject a DB failure (constraint violation or connection timeout) after the first INSERT
Verify the DB transaction is fully rolled back
Verify NO domain event was published to the message broker
Verify the API returns a 500 with a safe error message (no SQL in response)
failure_path_tests.expected_result: Full rollback; no partial data; no spurious event published; safe error response

failure_path_tests.title: Duplicate POST /api/admin/auth/login request is idempotent
failure_path_tests.description: Send the same POST /api/admin/auth/login request twice with an identical idempotency key. Verify the second call returns the same result without creating a duplicate record or publishing a second event.
steps: Send POST /api/admin/auth/login with idempotency key 'KEY-001'
Verify the first call succeeds and creates the resource
Send the identical POST /api/admin/auth/login again with the same 'KEY-001' key
Verify the second call returns the same response (200/201) without a new DB record
Verify only ONE domain event was published total
failure_path_tests.expected_result: Second call is a no-op; exactly one DB record; exactly one event published

result.feature_understanding: The admin login screen lets admin users sign in to access the admin panel. No specific business rules are identified for this feature in the documentation. It connects to the POST /api/admin/auth/login API for authentication. Also check the forgot‑password and token‑refresh flows as edge cases.

security_scenarios.title: CSRF attempt on admin logout endpoint
preconditions: Admin user is authenticated and has a valid session cookie

Auto‑submit the form when the victim visits the malicious page
Observe the HTTP response from the logout request
security_scenarios.expected_result: 403 Forbidden — logout request is rejected because the anti‑CSRF token is missing or invalid

security_scenarios.title: CSRF attempt on admin password reset endpoint
preconditions: Victim has a valid password‑reset token (e.g., from a password‑reset email)
Attacker hosts a malicious page on a different origin
steps: From the malicious page, submit a POST request to /api/admin/auth/reset-password with the victim's reset token and a new password, omitting any CSRF protection
Inspect the response status and body
security_scenarios.expected_result: 403 Forbidden — request is blocked due to missing or invalid CSRF token

security_scenarios.title: Login failure should not expose internal details
preconditions: Admin login page is reachable

steps: Send a POST request to /api/admin/auth/login with a valid email but an incorrect password
Capture the HTTP response body and status code
security_scenarios.expected_result: HTTP 401 Unauthorized (or 400) with a generic error message such as "Invalid credentials"; no stack trace, SQL statements, or file paths are returned

security_scenarios.title: Brute‑force protection on admin login
preconditions: Admin login endpoint is accessible
No prior lockout for the test account
steps: Rapidly send 100 POST requests to /api/admin/auth/login with random or sequential passwords (e.g., 1 request per second)
Monitor the responses for status codes
security_scenarios.expected_result: After a configurable threshold (e.g., 5‑10 failed attempts), the server returns HTTP 429 Too Many Requests and temporarily blocks further attempts; successful logins are not possible during the block period

security_scenarios.title: Non‑admin user attempting to access admin login endpoint
preconditions: A regular (non‑admin) user account exists with valid credentials

result.feature_understanding: The admin login screen lets administrators sign into the admin panel of the HKM Prasadam System. Testers must verify that only valid admin credentials are accepted and that any invalid or non‑admin attempts are rejected. The screen uses the POST /api/admin/auth/login API to perform authentication. The biggest risk is that the login could mistakenly grant access to unauthorized users or fail to block bad credentials, so both successful and failure scenarios need thorough testing. It’s also worth checking the forgot‑password and token‑refresh flows as edge cases.

result.feature_understanding: The admin login screen lets administrators sign in so they can reach the admin panel and manage the system. Testers must verify that only valid admin credentials are accepted and that any invalid attempt is blocked. This screen uses the POST /api/admin/auth/login API to authenticate users. The most critical risk is that a broken login could expose the admin area or lock out legitimate admins, so checking both successful and failed login flows is essential. Also be sure to test the password‑forgot flow (POST /api/admin/password/forgot) and token refresh scenarios, as they can behave differently from the normal login.

Verify the first call succeeds and creates the resource
Send the identical POST /api/admin/auth/login again with the same 'KEY-001' key
Verify the second call returns the same response (200/201) without a new DB record
Verify only ONE domain event was published total
failure_path_tests.expected_result: Second call is a no-op; exactly one DB record; exactly one event published

story: As an admin I want to log in to the dashboard"

result.feature_understanding: An admin logs in and opens the Live Dashboard to see real‑time registrations, coupons issued, bulk requests and slot fill rates. The dashboard must always show an alert for any pending bulk order approvals as soon as they exist. The biggest thing to verify is that the dashboard refreshes dynamically and all metrics update correctly when new bookings are made or filters are applied. Test also that the alert disappears correctly when there are no pending bulk orders, which can be a tricky edge case.

story: admin login and authenticatio test cases

result.feature_understanding: The admin authentication feature lets admin users sign in, stay logged in, refresh tokens, view their profile, and log out. A key rule is that an admin session must automatically expire after the configured period of inactivity. This feature connects to the authentication APIs: POST /api/admin/auth/login, POST /api/admin/auth/logout, POST /api/admin/auth/refresh, GET /api/admin/auth/me, and POST /api/admin/auth/forgot-password. The biggest risk is that a session might not expire or that unauthorized users could access admin pages, so testing session timeout and access control is critical. Also verify that non‑admin users are blocked from admin URLs and that the password‑reset flow handles invalid or missing data correctly.

story: admin login and authentication test cases

result.feature_understanding: This feature is about testing the admin login and authentication process, which is used by administrators to access the system. The most important thing to know is that there are specific APIs like POST /api/admin/login and POST /api/admin/logout that handle the login and logout functionality. This feature connects to the APIs mentioned, such as POST /api/admin/login, to authenticate the admin users. The biggest risk is that if the authentication is not properly tested, it could lead to security issues like unauthorized access, which is why testing for proper session expiration and validation is crucial. Additionally, edge cases like session expiration after inactivity and validation of user input should also be thoroughly tested to ensure the system's security and integrity.

story: admin login and authentication test cases

result.feature_understanding: This feature is about admin login and authentication, which is used by administrators to access the system. The most important thing to know is that there are specific APIs like POST /api/admin/login that handle the authentication process. This feature connects to the APIs such as POST /api/admin/login and POST /api/admin/authenticate to manage admin sessions. The biggest risk is that if the authentication is not properly tested, it could lead to security issues like unauthorized access, so it's crucial to test the login and session expiration thoroughly. Additionally, edge cases like session expiration after inactivity and validation of user input are also important to test to ensure the system is secure and functions as expected.

result.feature_understanding: Admin users can open the Default Settings page from the side navigation and set meal rates for Breakfast, Lunch and Dinner, define slot limits for each meal at each location, and configure auto‑open and auto‑close booking window rules. Only authorized admins may access this page and all numeric fields must accept only valid positive numbers; the system must reject negative values. The most critical test is to verify that saving any changes shows a success confirmation and that the saved values (rates, limits, toggles) are persisted and reflected in booking availability. Be careful to check that the auto‑close toggle does not reset after a page refresh and that a success message is always displayed, as bugs have been reported for these cases.

result.feature_understanding: The admin screen lets authorized admin users view and manage dashboards, registrations, settings and other admin functions. Only users with admin privileges may access these pages; any non‑admin attempt must be denied. The feature uses the authentication APIs such as POST /api/auth/login, POST /api/auth/logout, POST /api/auth/refresh-token and the admin profile endpoints. The biggest risk is that authentication or role checks fail, allowing unauthorized users to see or change admin data. Test the token refresh and logout flows to ensure a session cannot be reused after logout or expiration.

result.feature_understanding: The admin login screen lets users with admin privileges sign into the system so they can manage the dashboard, registrations, and settings. Testers must verify that an admin must be authenticated before any admin panel functions are accessible. The screen calls the POST /api/admin/auth/login endpoint to validate credentials. The most critical test is confirming that valid credentials allow access while invalid credentials are rejected, because a broken login blocks all admin work.

result.feature_understanding: The admin login page feature allows administrators to access the system, and it's used by admins to manage various aspects of the HKM Prasadam System. There are no specific business rules mentioned, but testers should be aware that the feature is critical and has a high severity. This feature connects to APIs such as POST /api/admin/login and GET /api/admin/session, which are used for authentication. The biggest risk is that the login page may not function correctly, allowing unauthorized access or preventing legitimate admins from logging in. Additionally, an edge case to consider is that non-admin users should not be able to access the admin panel via a direct URL, as mentioned in one of the bugs.

result.feature_understanding: This feature is about the admin login page, which administrators use to access the system. The key thing to remember is that admins log in using their email and password. This feature connects to the authentication module, which has APIs like POST /api/admin/login. The biggest risk is ensuring that only authorized admins can access the system, so testing the login functionality and access control is crucial. Additionally, testers should also verify that non-admin users are blocked from accessing admin pages, as indicated in some of the test cases.

result.feature_understanding: This feature is a payment screen in the admin panel that allows authorized admins to review and manage payment submissions. The key thing to remember is that only authorized admins should be able to access and manage these submissions, and they should be able to approve or decline payments based on the submitted details and screenshots. This feature connects to the payments module through APIs such as GET /api/admin/payments and PUT /api/admin/payments/{paymentId}. The biggest risk is that the payment approval or rejection process may not work correctly, leading to incorrect payment statuses or counts on the dashboard. One edge case to watch out for is that approved or declined payments should no longer show approval or rejection action buttons, which has been a known issue in the past.

result.feature_understanding: This feature is used by admins to review and manage payment submissions in the admin panel, allowing them to approve or decline payments. The key thing to remember is that only authorized admins can access and manage these payments, and once a payment is approved or declined, the status and counts should update accordingly. This feature connects to the payments module through APIs such as GET /api/admin/payments and PUT /api/admin/payments/{paymentId}. The biggest risk is that the payment status and counts may not update correctly, or the approve and reject buttons may not work as expected, so it's crucial to test these scenarios thoroughly. Additionally, there are known issues with the search function and verified count updates, so these areas will require extra attention during testing.

result.feature_understanding: The Payment tab shows booking details, a QR code for UPI payment and lets a pilgrim upload a screenshot of the transaction, while admins can view those details and approve them to change the status to Verified. The upload must be only JPG, PNG, or PDF and cannot be larger than 5 MB. The feature calls the GET /api/payments/tab endpoint to retrieve the payment information. The most critical test is to ensure the file‑type and size validation works and that approving a payment correctly updates the status to Verified and the verified count. Test an upload that is exactly 5 MB or uses an unsupported format to confirm the system rejects it as expected.

story: payment tab in admin screen test cases

result.feature_understanding: The payment tab in the admin screen lets administrators view and manage payment records, including booking IDs, pilgrim names, amounts, and screenshot previews. When an admin clicks Approve, the payment status must change to Verified and the Verified count on the dashboard must increment. This feature talks to the Payments module APIs such as GET /api/admin/payments and POST /api/admin/payments/{paymentId}/capture. The biggest risk is that the Verified count may not update after approval, which can hide successful verifications. Test also that searching by Booking ID returns only the exact record, because a known issue shows wrong results.

story: party booking form in public page

result.feature_understanding: The public party booking form lets any visitor submit a party enquiry with their name, mobile, optional email, event date, delivery address, meal counts and menu choice. The form must reject an event date that is less than seven days from today and must require a minimum of ten total plates across breakfast, lunch and dinner. When the form is submitted it calls the POST /api/parties/bookings endpoint to create the booking. The biggest risk is the validation logic for the date and plate‑count rules, so testers need to verify that invalid dates or insufficient plates are blocked. It’s also important to test the boundary cases, such as an event date exactly seven days ahead and a total of exactly ten plates, to ensure they are accepted.

story: party enquiry tab in admin screen

result.feature_understanding: The Party Enquiries tab is part of the admin screen and lets admins view, search, filter and update party enquiry requests. Admins can only change a pending enquiry’s status to Accepted or Declined, and the related counts must update in the summary cards. The list is populated from the GET /api/party‑enquiries endpoint, which supports mobile number and status filters. The biggest risk is that status values or required columns (such as Estimated Amount) may be missing or shown incorrectly, so verify that all three statuses and all expected columns appear. Also be sure that searches by Enquiry ID, Customer name or Mobile number return the correct results and that filtering by a status shows only enquiries with that status.

story: internal order tab in admin screen

result.feature_understanding: The internal orders tab lets an admin view, search, and manage internal orders in the admin screen. Only orders that have been accepted can be marked as Delivered; other rows must not allow the Deliver action. The tab pulls data from the admin internal‑orders API endpoints such as GET /api/admin/internal-orders and the related GET, POST, PUT, and PATCH calls. The most important thing to test is that the status column and delivery badge update correctly when an order is marked Delivered and that the summary cards reflect the new totals. Also check that searching by Order ID returns the correct row and that all required columns remain visible when filters like mobile or date are applied.

result.feature_understanding: The admin login screen lets admin users sign in using their email and password. If the credentials are incorrect the system must show the exact error message. This screen connects to the POST /api/admin/auth/login API. The biggest risk is that invalid logins might not display the correct error or could allow access to the admin dashboard without proper authentication. Test that leaving the email or password blank is handled correctly and does not allow a login.

result.feature_understanding: The admin dashboard shows live metrics and alerts for users with the admin role. It must automatically refresh its data so that counts for total registrations, coupons issued, bulk requests and meal slot fill rates are always current. The dashboard gets its information from the GET /api/admin/dashboard API. The biggest risk is that the dynamic refresh or the pending‑bulk‑approval alert could fail to update, showing stale or missing data. Test the date and location filters and verify the bulk‑approval alert appears correctly when pending bulk orders exist.

result.feature_understanding: The Live Dashboard in the admin panel shows key metrics and alerts for admin users. The dashboard must refresh automatically and display real‑time data, including an alert when a pending bulk approval exists. It gets its information from the GET /api/admin/dashboard API. The biggest risk is that the data does not update instantly or the bulk‑approval alert fails to appear when required. Also check that date and location filters correctly change the displayed metrics, especially when the filter results in no data.

result.feature_understanding: The Dashboard module shows live booking and registration information for admin users who manage locations and slot settings. Admins must be able to filter the dashboard by location and see alerts for pending bulk approvals, otherwise critical data is hidden. The biggest risk is that the location filter and bulk‑approval alerts may not work, causing the displayed data to remain unchanged or missing. Also verify that searching registrations by a valid name returns results and that the filter correctly isolates data for each selected location.

event_flow.data: The entity being created, updated, or deleted

event_flow.data: Event payload containing the updated entity data and a correlation ID
event_flow.validation_point: Event is published only after the database transaction commits (outbox pattern). No event is emitted if the transaction fails. Failed deliveries are routed to a dead-letter queue for investigation.

event_flow.data: Consumed event payload
event_flow.validation_point: Processing is idempotent — running the same event twice produces the same result. Failures trigger retries and ultimately land in a dead-letter queue. Message ordering is preserved where the business logic requires it.

event_flow.data: Notification message containing the action result
event_flow.validation_point: The notification is sent to the correct recipient only. The right template and channel are used for the event type. No duplicate notifications are sent if the event is retried. No personal or sensitive data is exposed in the notification body or subject line.

result.feature_understanding: The payment tab is used by admin users to view pending payments, see details such as booking ID, pilgrim name and amount, and then approve or reject each payment. Approving must change the payment status to Verified and update the verified count, rejecting must change it to Declined and update the declined count, and the approve/reject buttons must disappear after a decision is made. This feature works with the Payments module APIs, for example GET /api/payments/methods and POST /api/payments/checkout. The biggest risk is that status changes, count updates, or button visibility may not behave correctly, so testers should verify the status, counts and button state after each action. Testers should also confirm that only JPG, PNG or PDF files can be uploaded as screenshots and that the upload area opens the file browser.
